# Judgewright

> A free tool by Nor AI Technologies (https://norai.tech), an engineering studio in Ghazipur, India that builds custom AI, web and 3D software delivered into the customer's own infrastructure. Judgewright is a free, in-browser tool that checks whether an LLM-as-judge agrees with human labels once chance is removed. Paste JSONL or CSV rows with an example id, the judge's label and the human label; it returns a plain verdict, Cohen's kappa with a seeded bootstrap interval, Krippendorff's alpha, a confusion matrix and every disagreement. Nothing is uploaded and no account is needed.

## Use it

- [Judgewright](https://judge.norai.tech/tools/judgewright): the tool. Paste verdict rows or load a sample set.

## What it computes

- Raw agreement, the always-majority chance baseline, and unweighted Cohen's kappa on one shared scale, with the gap between raw agreement and kappa stated in percentage points.
- A seeded, reproducible bootstrap confidence interval for kappa, accuracy and alpha. The replicate count is tiered by row count and printed.
- Krippendorff's alpha with the judge as a panel member, and a humans-only alpha (the ceiling) when rows carry two or more human labels.
- Linear and quadratic weighted kappa as secondary readings for ordered labels.
- ECE and Brier score when a judge_score column is present; position and length bias when pairwise columns are present.
- A receipt with the formula and exact inputs, so a reviewer can recompute kappa by hand.

## Input format

- JSONL: one object per line with example_id, judge_label, human_label. Optional: human_labels (array), judge_score, judge_critique, human_critique, position, preferred_longer.
- CSV with the same columns; common aliases (label, prediction, gold_label, confidence) are mapped automatically.

## Limits

- It does not run a judge or call any model. You bring the verdicts.
- It keeps no history across runs.
- Grade bands are the Landis–Koch convention, a convenience mapping rather than a standard.
